Earlier this month, following last week's release of a carrier settings update to address cellular network issues affecting certain iPhone 18 Pro Max users on the AT&T network, Apple is now rolling out another carrier bundle update for devices running iOS 27.2 beta. Here are the details.

Apple updates AT&T carrier bundle for iOS 27.2 beta

Last Friday, Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max users on the AT&T network were experiencing an issue that could cause their devices to lose cellular service and be unable to make calls.

Apple stated that iOS 27.0.1, along with a new carrier settings update, should have prevented the issue from affecting more devices. However, iPhones that had already lost service still required a hardware replacement.

Tonight, as spotted by Aaron Perris on X, Apple began rolling out another carrier bundle update for iPhone 18 Pro Max users on the AT&T network, this time specifically targeting devices running iOS 27.2 beta.

Reports of the issue first surfaced in late September, when some iPhone 18 Pro Max users on the AT&T network found that their devices suddenly could not make calls, send or receive text messages, or use mobile data, with the status bar showing only "SOS".

It is worth noting that the issue only affected the iPhone 18 Pro Max, which uses a Qualcomm modem in the United States. The iPhone 18 Pro, which uses Apple's own C2 modem, was not affected.

The carrier settings update Apple released last week upgraded AT&T users running iOS 27.0 to version 72.1. However, users running iOS 27.2 beta remained on the older 72.0.2 carrier bundle.

According to reports, tonight's release upgrades those devices to carrier bundle version 72.0.3, presumably extending Apple's AT&T carrier settings changes to iPhone 18 Pro Max users testing the iOS 27.2 beta.
